brief.headline: Memory supercycle intact—HBM tight, DRAM/NAND contracts +58–75% QoQ Q2, hyperscalers hit $700B capex, CoWoS easing but still 10% short
brief.summary: <cite index="11-2,11-7">Conventional DRAM contract prices surged 58–63% QoQ in Q2 2026, with NAND Flash up 70–75% QoQ</cite>, sustaining the historic spike from Q1's 90–95% DRAM jump. <cite index="3-2,3-3">HBM3E trades at ~$300/stack, HBM3 at ~$200/stack, with SK Hynix commanding 50–55% market share</cite>, while <cite index="1-9,1-11">supply remains constrained through 2026 and lead times for HBM3E sit at 20–26 weeks</cite>. <cite index="20-3,21-2,21-6">Hyperscalers now top $700 billion in 2026 AI capex, up from $400 billion in 2025</cite>, driving structural wafer reallocation away from commodity memory. <cite index="29-4,29-6">TSMC CoWoS supply-demand gap is narrowing from 20% to ~10% by year-end as monthly capacity hits 120,000–140,000 wafers</cite>, though <cite index="35-1,35-7">Nvidia secures over 60% of total CoWoS for 2025–2026</cite>. <cite index="39-2,39-3">Samsung and SK Hynix are preparing to unveil a combined $646 billion investment package on Monday</cite>, signaling long-cycle capacity commitments.
brief.pair_trade_view: <cite index="40-5,40-6">SK Hynix recently surpassed Samsung as South Korea's most valuable listed company at ~$1.35 trillion market cap, driven by its dominance in the HBM market that Nvidia desperately needs</cite>. <cite index="43-8">Samsung held 35% HBM market share in Q3 2025 vs SK Hynix's 53%</cite>, but <cite index="43-8">customers now say 'Samsung is back' on HBM4</cite>. SK Hynix remains the pure-play beneficiary of AI memory with higher operating leverage to HBM ASP expansion, while Samsung offers diversification drag but improving qualification momentum. <cite index="41-8,41-9">Samsung trades at 8.1x 2026E P/E vs SK Hynix at 9.2x</cite>, both deeply discounted vs global peers, but SK Hynix earns the scarcity premium. Near-term, Samsung catching Nvidia qualification and OpenAI Stargate supply could compress the relative multiple gap; structurally, SK Hynix's HBM mix advantage persists. Relative: neutral to slight SK Hynix overweight until Samsung demonstrates sustained HBM4 volume ramp.

memory_cycle.notes: <cite index="16-1,16-6,16-8">DRAM and NAND are in a structural reallocation to HBM, not a cyclical shortage—memory broke in 2025 and the assumption of normalization on the usual cycle is wrong, with prices elevated through 2027 and the long-term floor reset higher</cite>. <cite index="18-25">HBM's 3-to-1 wafer consumption ratio vs DDR5 means every HBM ramp directly compresses general-purpose memory supply</cite>. <cite index="12-34,16-18">2026 DRAM supply growth projected at just 16% YoY and NAND at 17% YoY, well below 20–30% historical norms</cite>. <cite index="16-26,16-27,16-28">SK Hynix HBM/DRAM/NAND sold out through 2026, Micron CEO cited supply tightness into 2027, and every NAND manufacturer reportedly sold out 2026 capacity</cite>. Pricing momentum decelerating from Q1 peak but no reversal visible; <cite index="17-10,17-11,17-12">buyers hesitant to chase higher spot quotes and NAND spot trading quiet, signaling parabolic phase maturing into plateau rather than peak</cite>. New fab capacity arrives late 2027–2028 earliest. Capex discipline from Samsung/SK Hynix prevents panic supply response.

brief.hbm_pulse: <cite index="1-1,1-2">HBM now represents 30–40% of total AI accelerator manufacturing cost, up from under 20% two generations ago; for the B200 with eight HBM3e stacks, memory alone costs $2,400, exceeding logic die cost</cite>. <cite index="8-1">Samsung and SK Hynix raised HBM3E supply prices by nearly 20% for 2026</cite>, and <cite index="6-1,6-3,6-5">server DDR5 profitability has overtaken HBM since early 2026—a historic first—with constrained capacity and rising conventional DRAM margins giving suppliers stronger leverage, pushing 2027 HBM ASP sharply higher</cite>. <cite index="8-2,8-3">HBM3E supply remains tight as Samsung and SK Hynix prioritize ramping HBM4; 2026 revenue mix forecast at ~55% HBM4 and 45% HBM3E, with HBM4 starting Q3 to rapidly absorb prior HBM3E demand</cite>. <cite index="12-20">Micron CEO projects HBM market growing from $35B in 2025 to $100B by 2028</cite>. Supply severely constrained: <cite index="2-20">Nvidia reportedly accounts for the majority of SK Hynix HBM output through 2026</cite>, and <cite index="43-1,43-5">Samsung/SK Hynix signed LOI with OpenAI for eventual 900,000 DRAM wafers/month for Stargate project</cite>. HBM remains the choke point; pricing power intact into 2027.

news_pulse.headline: Samsung, SK Hynix preparing $646B investment unveil Monday—largest in Korean history
news_pulse.implication: Signals decade-long capacity commitment (1,000 trillion won over 10 years for Samsung Group) and second major chip cluster buildout in South Korea. Blue House briefing Monday with top execs confirms state backing. Validates structural view on memory cycle durability but also flags risk of 2034–35 delivery timeline requiring sustained AI demand. Watch for government backstops vs pure corporate capex risk.

news_pulse.headline: Q2 2026 DRAM contracts +58–63% QoQ, NAND +70–75% QoQ—NAND now rising faster than DRAM
news_pulse.implication: First time NAND outpaces DRAM in current cycle, driven by enterprise SSD demand for generative AI deployments. Q1 saw record 90–95% DRAM QoQ; rate of increase slowing but no reversal. Confirms suppliers maintaining pricing discipline and CSPs locking long-term agreements. Meaningful capacity expansion unlikely until late 2027.

news_pulse.headline: Hyperscaler 2026 capex hits $700B, up 77% YoY—Meta raises guide to $125–145B
news_pulse.implication: Amazon ~$200B, Microsoft ~$190B, Alphabet $175–185B, Meta $115–135B. Meta's upward revision citing higher component pricing and data center costs triggered 9.25% share drop Thursday—first investor rebellion against spending curve. Roughly 75% allocated to AI infrastructure (GPUs, HBM servers, networking). Sustains structural demand for HBM/server DRAM but raises ROI uncertainty for hyperscalers. Bottleneck shifting from Nvidia allocation to power/grid interconnects.

news_pulse.headline: TSMC CoWoS supply-demand gap narrowing to 10% by end-2026 from 20% today
news_pulse.implication: Monthly CoWoS capacity reaching 120,000–140,000 wafers in 2026, with OSATs adding 50,000–60,000, approaching 200K/month industry total. TSMC forecasts CoWoS CAGR >80% from 2022–2027. Nvidia locked 60% of 2025–26 capacity. Easing bottleneck is bullish for AI accelerator supply but implies Nvidia/AMD share more dependent on HBM allocation than packaging by H2. Samsung/SK Hynix HBM supply becomes the new constraint.

news_pulse.headline: SK Hynix overtakes Samsung as South Korea's most valuable company at $1.35T market cap
news_pulse.implication: Market repricing values SK Hynix's 53% HBM market share and HBM expertise over Samsung's diversified business. Reflects HBM scarcity premium and SK Hynix's pure-play leverage to AI memory demand. Stocks still cheap: Samsung 8.1x 2026E P/E, SK Hynix 9.2x vs global top-30 peers. SK Securities calls them 'cheapest stocks in the age of AI' with expected valuation rerating and narrowing of Korea discount.

news_pulse.headline: Server DDR5 profitability overtook HBM in early 2026—historic first per TrendForce
news_pulse.implication: Rapid ASP escalation in server DDR5 driven by capacity reallocation to HBM has flipped margin hierarchy. CSP long-term contracts with floor pricing clauses limit downside for suppliers. Implies 2027 HBM ASP will push sharply higher as suppliers have stronger leverage. Validates pricing power sustainability and margin expansion runway for Samsung/SK Hynix.

news_pulse.headline: Single-stock leverage ETFs on Samsung/SK Hynix hit 17.6T won AUM, 35% of daily ETF volume
news_pulse.implication: Retail frenzy in 2x leverage products driving KOSPI volatility spikes: 7 days with >5% index moves since listing, 11 sidecar triggers, 3 circuit breakers. VKOSPI (fear gauge) hit all-time high 92.71 on June 26. Short gamma structure amplifying swings. Financial authorities preparing investor protection measures. Macro structure risk for both names—watch for regulatory intervention or forced deleveraging episodes.

news_pulse.headline: KOSPI slides 10% intraday June 23, Samsung/SK Hynix down >12% before circuit breaker
news_pulse.implication: Violent profit-taking from record highs; 20-minute trading suspension implemented. Reflects extreme positioning, leverage ETF amplification, and global tech selloff contagion. Both stocks rebounded but remain volatile. Fundamentals intact but technical setup fragile. Intraday volatility likely persists until leverage product regulation or positioning washout.

brief.derivatives_signal: Extreme volatility regime. VKOSPI all-time high 92.71 (June 26) vs 70.78 one month prior, driven by single-stock leverage ETF proliferation (17.6T won AUM, 35–40% of daily ETF volume). Short gamma dynamics from 2x products amplifying intraday swings; circuit breakers triggered 3x in past month. June 23 saw 10% KOSPI intraday plunge with >12% Samsung/SK Hynix drops before suspension. Retail positioning stretched after YTD surge. Implied vol elevated but realized vol higher—term structure likely inverted. Options flow skewed to upside call buying (leverage ETF rebalancing) but downside tail risk mispriced. Near-term: fade parabolic moves, leg into long vol on dips. Structural play remains long equity with tail hedges; leverage products face regulatory overhang.

Any TrendForce or DRAMeXchange spot price updates for late-June DDR4/DDR5—watch if buyer hesitancy flagged last week translates to spot price deceleration
Hyperscaler earnings commentary follow-through (Meta FCF collapse, Amazon capex sustain) and any enterprise AI revenue guidance revisions
Korean financial regulator announcements on leverage ETF restrictions or margin requirement changes post-VKOSPI spike
TSMC CoWoS June delivery data or NVIDIA Blackwell shipment updates—any signs packaging constraint fully cleared would shift bottleneck back to HBM supply (bullish Samsung/SK Hynix)
